043package dev.visdb.seesaw.datasources;
044
045import java.sql.JDBCType;
046import java.sql.SQLException;
047
048import javax.sql.RowSet;
049
050import dev.visdb.seesaw.formatting.SsFormat;
051import dev.visdb.seesaw.navigate.RowsModel;
052
053/**
054 * This interface is an accessor to a {@linkplain RowSet} and one of its
055 * columns; it is extended by {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.utils.SsComponent}.
056 * Some components, in particular {@linkplain dev.visdb.seesaw.SsTable},
057 * have multiple columns; this
058 * interface allows a lightweight object to provide row set access for
059 * a specified column. Many
060 * methods can declare a {@linkplain RSC} parameter instead of a
061 * {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.utils.SsComponent}.
062 */
063// TODO: getAllowNull() is an issue
064// TODO: some of these must carefully be specified to only use a subset of the
065//       methods. The getColumn[Text/Object] could be problematic.
066//      They should have a way to check for recursion.
067public interface RSC {
068  /**
069   * Construct and return an object representing a RowsModel column.
070   * <p>
071   * TODO: SO FAR ONLY USED WITH/FROM GRID. Issue with getColumnObject undo/redo.
072   * @param rowsModel
073   * @param columnIndex
074   * @return
075   * @throws SqlRuntimeException
076   */
077  static RSC get(RowsModel rowsModel, int columnIndex) {
078    //
079    // TODO: accept format, implement in SimpleRSC
080    //
081    try {
082      return new SimpleRSC(rowsModel, columnIndex);
083    } catch (SQLException ex) {
084      throw new SqlRuntimeException(ex);
085    }
086  }
087
088  /**
089   * Construct and return an object representing a RowSet column.
090   * <p>
091   * TODO: NOT USED
092   * @param rowsModel
093   * @param columnIndex
094   * @return
095   * @throws java.sql.SQLException
096   */
097  static RSC getEx(RowsModel rowsModel, int columnIndex) throws SQLException {
098    return new SimpleRSC(rowsModel, columnIndex);
099  }
100
101  /**
102   * Construct and return an object representing a RowSet column.
103   * <p>
104   * TODO: NOT USED
105   * @param rowsModel
106   * @param columnName
107   * @return
108   * @throws java.sql.SQLException
109   */
110  static RSC getEx(RowsModel rowsModel, String columnName) throws SQLException {
111    return new SimpleRSC(rowsModel, columnName);
112  }
113
114  /**
115   * @return the RowsModel
116   */
117  RowsModel getRowsModel();
118
119  /**
120   * @return the row set
121   */
122  RowSet getRowSet();
123
124  /**
125   * @return the column index in the rowset
126   */
127  int getColumnIndex();
128
129  /**
130   * @return the column name in the rowset
131   */
132  String getColumnName();
133
134  /**
135   * @return The JDBCType of the column in the rowset
136   */
137  JDBCType getColumnJDBCType();
138
139  /**
140   * @return column value as a String
141   */
142  String getColumnText();
143  //Object getColumnObject() throws SQLException;
144
145  /**
146   * Returns an Object of the specified type
147   * representing the value in the bound database column.
148   *
149   * Note a null is never converted into ""; use getColumnText for that.
150   * @param <T> type to return
151   * @param clazz Class of returned type
152   * @return column object
153   */
154  <T> T getColumnObject(Class<T> clazz);
155  //<T> T getTypedObject() throws SQLException;
156
157  /**
158   * A component may have a display/parse format.
159   * @return The format for this component
160   */
161  default SsFormat getSsFormat() {
162    return null;
163  }
164
165  /**
166   * @return Does the column allow null?
167   */
168  boolean getAllowNull();
169
170  /**
171   * @return typically column name wrapped in "[]"
172   */
173  String getColumnForLog();
174}
